display.purpose: The one largest thing on a page. Familjen Grotesk in the app.

headline.purpose: Section titles; floored at 1.75rem so a phone keeps a display step.

title.purpose: A heading on a card. 20px, the step eight routes used to hand-roll.

body.purpose: Hanken Grotesk; everything the interface says at reading size.

label.purpose: Spline Sans Mono, uppercase, 0.16em. Anything the pipeline emitted.

arabic.purpose: Readex Pro; takes both the display and body roles under RTL, at 1.85 leading and no negative tracking.

marketing-display.purpose: Bricolage Grotesque, scoped to .world-dark and .world-light only, variable across opsz.

shadows.name: soft
shadows.purpose: A sheet resting on the board. Default for cards and standing panels.

shadows.name: lifted
shadows.purpose: A sheet picked up: interactive hover, the auth sheet.

shadows.name: primary
shadows.purpose: The primary control's weight. Offset and blur, never a halo.

shadows.name: primary-hover
shadows.purpose: Primary control hover: it lifts further, it does not glow.

shadows.name: lit-inset
shadows.purpose: The single hairline a control carries on the board.

shadows.name: soft-night
shadows.purpose: The same lift in the studio after dark.

shadows.name: marketing-primary
shadows.value: 0 0 0 1px color-mix(in srgb, #7240ff 20%, transparent), 0 2px 18px -6px color-mix(in srgb, #7240ff 60%, transparent), 0 0 44px -10px color-mix(in srgb, #7240ff 32%, transparent)
shadows.purpose: .world-dark only: the control's own light, centred halos rather than a drop shadow.

motion.name: ease-out-soft
motion.purpose: Entrances and hover lifts: arrive fast, settle.

motion.name: stagger-step
motion.purpose: List arrivals without a JS timeline.

motion.name: reduced-motion-feedback
motion.value: 120ms on color, background-color, border-color, box-shadow, opacity
motion.purpose: Motion is removed; the interface still answers.

narrative.overview:
A dry studio board in daylight, with sheets of work laid on it. The Darkroom that preceded it argued that a near-black room lets the print be the only lit thing; that is a good idea about photographs and the wrong one about brands. You cannot judge a colour in the dark, and most generated brands are drawn on light paper, so a near-black chrome forced every specimen into a bright rectangle in a void. The board is the answer: a warm matte ground (#e7e3da), white sheets on it, and shadow rather than light doing the lifting. [data-theme='dark'] is the same studio after dark, not an inversion.

The Darkroom did not die, it was scoped. .world-dark is the retained marketing world on /, /pricing, /brand-kit and the legal pages, because the brand is dark on purpose. .world-light is the guest scope: a region handed to a generated brand, painted in the customer's own checked ink. The app itself is the board, arriving as a :root scope while twenty-three routes migrate onto it one at a time.

The board has three registers, and the boundary is one question: does this surface show something the product generated? Wall (generated work pinned up: sheets, cast shadows, gaps visible), Bench (one thing at working size with tools at its edges), Desk (squared to a grid, never pinned, tabular figures). Nothing generated is ever tabulated; nothing financial is ever pinned.
keyCharacteristics: Warm matte ground, white sheets, warm shadows — never a blue or black shadow
One accent ramp, pinned to the logo, and used as little as possible
Depth by cast shadow and tonal step, not by glow
Five faces with five jobs; the mono face is the machine's voice
Every colour under text carries a measured contrast number in the source
Three registers with a one-question boundary

rules.name: The One Ramp Rule
rules.body: There is no second accent. Status colours aside, anything that needs emphasis borrows from Signal Violet, Bridge Indigo and Signal Blue.

rules.name: The Readable Accent Rule
rules.body: Signal Violet is 4.21:1 on the board — enough under a control, not under words. So accent text is #5b33cc in daylight and #aa8cff at night. In .world-dark it is #aa8cff at 7.57:1. The value differs either side; the ramp does not.

rules.name: The Ink Light Rule
rules.body: On the board, decorative light is drawn in ink, not in the accent. --accent-surface is re-pointed at ink at 13%, which moves lit, bloom, rail, rail-node and pulse-ring in one declaration. Left pointing at the ramp, every card wore a violet gradient along its bottom and the accent stopped meaning 'this matters' the moment it appeared on all of them.

rules.name: The Checked Tone Rule
rules.body: Every colour this system puts under text is verified against the ground it will actually sit on, not against the friendliest one, and the measured number is recorded next to the token. A muted token with no headroom is a token that fails wherever a surface is tinted at all.

rules.name: The Guest Palette Rule
rules.body: On any surface showing a generated brand, that brand supplies the colour. .world-light re-points the semantic chrome names at the --guest-* variables lib/brand-theme.ts emits. Nothing in that scope is a literal, greys are absent, and the ramp is deliberately absent — :focus-visible draws from --brand-primary, and a guest palette allowed to shadow it renders an invisible focus ring on its own section. Chrome tokens are not shadowable by untrusted input, and a generated palette is untrusted input even when it is our own example brand.

rules.name: The Committed Dark Rule
rules.body: The app follows the reader's theme; the marketing pages do not. .world-dark stays dark under [data-theme='light'] because the brand is dark by commitment, not by category default. The default theme is now daylight: the board's thesis is that a brand cannot be judged in the dark, so opening the product in a night room would ship the argument backwards.

rules.name: The Colour Arc Rule
rules.body: A marketing section is either chrome or it is a guest, never both. A section that hands itself to a generated brand takes that brand's whole palette, including its decorative light; a chrome section keeps ours.

rules.name: The World Ground Rule
rules.body: body:has(> .world-dark) paints the document #05070f. A world scope sits on a div, so it paints itself and its subtree — but the body is painted from the document's own tokens, which are the board's, and rubber-banding a dark marketing page revealed a warm board underneath it. The document takes its ground from the world its page actually opened in.

rules.name: The Machine Voice Rule
rules.body: Anything the pipeline emitted is set in Spline Sans Mono — credit figures, file dimensions, dates, hex codes, log lines, elapsed time. Anything we wrote is not. Nothing may set a weight heavier than 500 on it: the face has no bold to draw and the browser would synthesise one.

rules.name: The Isolated Value Rule
rules.body: A machine value inside a paragraph carries machine-value (direction: ltr; unicode-bidi: isolate). Inside an Arabic paragraph the bidi algorithm renders #1B3A3A as 1B3A3A# and /home as home/. A hex is something a customer copies and a route is something they type.

rules.name: The RTL Display Rule
rules.body: Under [dir='rtl'], both --font-display and --font-sans re-point to Readex Pro, at the variable rather than at the utilities. Appending the Arabic face to the Latin stack does not work: next/font's metric-adjusted fallback is declared local("Arial"), Arial has Arabic coverage, and it answers first. 451 Arabic glyphs were rendering in Arial before this.

rules.name: The Tracking Floor Rule
rules.body: One negative value, -0.02em, from title size upward and never below it. Arabic drops negative tracking entirely and takes its own leading.

rules.name: The Marketing Pairing Rule
rules.body: Bricolage Grotesque is declared on .world-dark, .world-light only. The app keeps one display family and the page that sells typography gets a pairing.

rules.name: The Register Boundary Rule
rules.body: Ask one question of a surface: does it show something the product generated? Yes → wall or bench. No → desk. Nothing generated is ever tabulated; nothing financial is ever pinned.

rules.name: The Tabular Figure Rule
rules.body: Every desk figure is tabular-nums. A column of credit balances or order totals that shifts horizontally between rows is a column nobody can scan.

rules.name: The Lifted Not Lit Rule
rules.body: A control on a board is lifted, not lit. --shadow-primary and --shadow-primary-hover exist as tokens precisely because the halo was three literals reading --brand-primary inline — the one lit thing a scope could not move, since the fill has to stay violet. On a dark ground that halo reads as light; on a board in daylight it reads as haze.

rules.name: The Light From The Horizon Rule (retired in the app, retained in marketing)
rules.body: It said: there is one light in this product, it is the arc rising behind the fold, and everything lit is lit from below. That is still exactly true inside .world-dark. It is dead on the board: a board in daylight has no horizon to rise from. The lit, bloom and radial-wash compositions were removed from the dashboard shell, the billing panel, the onboarding bench and the auth sheet rather than recoloured.

rules.name: The Tinted Shadow Rule
rules.body: No shadow in this system is pure black. Warm brown on the board, black-at-opacity at night, ink-mixed in a guest scope.

rules.name: The Rendered Light Rule
rules.body: Light is drawn, never faked with a decorative image. Anything that glows reads --accent-surface, so a scope can move all of it at once.

rules.name: The Lit Control Rule
rules.body: A Button always carries a source — a fill with a shadow, or the lit inner edges. A Badge never carries one: no fill gradient, no shadow, no lit edges, no border, no hover. Now that both are pills, the light is the only thing telling a control from a state.

rules.name: The Reduced Motion Rule
rules.body: prefers-reduced-motion removes motion and keeps feedback. Animations collapse to one frame and transforms are dropped, but colour, background, border, shadow and opacity keep transitioning at 120ms. The two states that exist only as movement get a still form instead of nothing: the shimmer becomes a steady tint, the pulse a static ring.

dos: Do ask the register question first: generated work goes on the wall or the bench; money and settings go on the desk.
Do lift a sheet with a warm cast shadow (rgba(60,52,38,…)) and a tonal step, never with a halo.
Do set accent text at #5b33cc in daylight and #aa8cff at night, and reserve #7240ff for fills, focus and edges.
Do set anything the pipeline emitted in Spline Sans Mono at 400 or 500, and wrap it in machine-value when it sits inside a sentence.
Do put every desk figure in tabular-nums.
Do measure a new text colour against the worst ground it will sit on and record the number in the source next to it.
Do reach for a semantic token (bg-surface, text-fg-muted, border-line) so a component re-skins by scope without being touched.
Do let a guest scope own its colour completely, including its decorative light.
donts: Don't draw the Darkroom's horizon on the board. No lit gradient edge, no bloom, no radial wash behind a header, no glow behind a form. There is nothing for light to rise from.
Don't point --accent-surface back at the ramp inside the app. A violet edge on every card is how the accent stops meaning anything.
Don't let a generated palette bind --brand-primary or any chrome token; --guest-* is the only namespace an untrusted palette may write.
Don't put Signal Violet under words on the board — 4.21:1 is a control's number, not a paragraph's.
Don't introduce a second accent hue. Status colours aside, emphasis borrows from the one ramp.
Don't set the mono face above weight 500; the browser will synthesise a bold that does not exist.
Don't use negative letter-spacing on Arabic, or leave --font-display pointing at a Latin-only face under RTL.
Don't give a Badge a shadow, a gradient or a hover — that makes it look like a control.
Don't draw a hard grey border in .world-dark; borders there are translucent white at 9% and 16%.
Don't run a decorative animation forever. Only a live generation and a loading skeleton loop.
Don't register a Tailwind colour named base; it compiles .text-base into a colour instead of a font size.
